goal: Wants to end statements with conviction instead of trailing off or upspeaking.
userTurn: I always trail off at the end of what I'm saying, like my voice goes up and it sounds like a question. How do I end strong?
emotionalSignal: self-aware, motivated — has correctly identified the pattern and wants the mechanism

recentReps.note: point was strong, then ended on 'so yeah...' with rising pitch

memoryState.structureRead: The most-recent rep's close trailed off — ended on 'so yeah' with a rising pitch rather than landing the final sentence as the point.

caseFormulation.hypothesis: keeps talking past the point — adds a trailing softener ('so yeah', 'anyway') instead of stopping on the strong sentence

expectedCoachMove: Name the specific mechanism from the STRUCTURE READ: he lands the point then keeps going, adding a trailing softener with rising pitch. The fix is to STOP on the strong sentence — end the sentence as the point and hold the silence, don't fill it. One concrete move (make the last sentence the ask, then stop; no 'so yeah'). Authoritative register: declarative.
badAnswerExample: Work on your confidence and projection! Practice ending sentences with a downward inflection. Record yourself and listen back. The more you practice, the more natural your strong endings will become. Believe in what you're saying!
excellentAnswerExample: The trail-off is a real thing you're doing: today you landed the point, then tacked on 'so yeah' with your pitch going up — that's what turns a statement into a question. You don't need a stronger voice, you need an earlier full stop. Make your last sentence the actual point, then stop on it. The silence after is the authority. Next rep: end on the point, resist the 'so yeah,' let it sit.
